memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'The priest shall burn the memorial portion of the crushed grain and the oil, together with all the incense, as a food offering presented to the LORD.'" - Lev 2:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends where it began — with a portion rising to God.

Look at what goes up: crushed grain, oil, and all the incense. Every bit of the incense burns. Nothing of it is kept back or eaten. Incense throughout Scripture is connected with prayer; the psalmist asked that his prayer be set before God like incense (Ps 141:2), and in Revelation the incense before God's throne is explicitly identified as the prayers of God's people (Rev 5:8).

So the picture that closes the grain offering is this: the fruit of a person's labour, the oil, and the whole of their prayer, ascending together to God and received with pleasure.

That is a fitting summary of a life offered to God. Not just what you produce. Not just what you give. But your work and your prayer rising together, inseparable — the daily grind and the daily conversation with God woven into one offering.

Many believers keep these apart. Prayer belongs to the quiet corner; work belongs to the world. Leviticus 2 puts them on the same altar.

Whatever your hands did this week, and whatever your heart said to God this week — bring both. God receives them as one gift.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I treat my work and my prayer life as two separate compartments?
2. What would it look like to offer today's work and today's prayers together to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, take the work of my hands and the prayers of my heart and receive them together. Let my whole ordinary life rise to You as a pleasing offering. Amen.
